extraction_notes: 10-K is unusually thin on Pentagon program-of-record disclosures. The company does NOT name any specific DoD Program Element (PE) numbers or named DoD programs of record (no Skyborg, CCA, SDA Tracking Layer, BQM-167, XQ-58, Project Maven, AFRL Quantum Networking, etc.). The only specific federal customer named is NASA, via subcontract through Analytical Mechanics Associates. Forward funding language references CHIPS Act and DOE Title 17 (Loan Programs Office) — both are aspirational, not booked. Total FY2023 revenue was only $358,047, so DoD revenue concentration is structurally low. We extract the few J-Book-adjacent claims (NASA subcontracts, CHIPS Act ambition, DOE Title 17 ambition) plus control claims (TFLN fab facility, patents, going-concern).

claims.claim_text: QCi was awarded a fourth NASA subcontract on Feb 14, 2024 to study sun-noise reduction in LIDAR images using the EQC; prime contractor is Analytical Mechanics Associates.
claims.subject: Quantum Computing Inc.
claims.source_quote: On February 14, 2024 the Company announced that it has been awarded a fourth subcontract with NASA to study sun noise reduction in LIDAR images using the EQC. The prime contractor for this award is Analytical Mechanics Associates.

claims.claim_text: QCi expects to apply for and receive funding under the DOE Title 17 Clean Energy Financing Program (managed by DOE Loan Programs Office) to support its TFLN chip manufacturing buildout in Tempe, AZ.
claims.subject: Quantum Computing Inc.
claims.object_value: DOE Title 17 Clean Energy Financing (Loan Programs Office)
claims.source_quote: The Company has plans to support this initiative by applying for funding for distinct uses under both the Title 17 Clean Energy Financing Program managed by the US Department of Energy's Loan Programs Office...

claims.claim_text: QCi expects to apply for and receive funding under the CHIPS Act ($52B allocation, of which $39B is manufacturing incentives and $13B is R&D) for its TFLN chip fab buildout.
claims.subject: Quantum Computing Inc.
claims.source_quote: ...also the Creating Helpful Incentives to Produce Semiconductors Act of 2022 (the CHIPS Act), which allocates $52 billion for the revitalization and onshoring of semiconductor manufacturing in the U.S.

claims.claim_text: QCi's core photonic / quantum / TFLN technology is positioned for DoD applications including LIDAR for aircraft/drones/satellites, photonic vibrometer for remote sensing (including space-based platforms), and quantum-secured authentication for network cybersecurity.
claims.subject: Quantum Computing Inc.
claims.source_quote: We expect subsequent photonic vibrometer versions, currently under development, to reach significantly greater distances, minimize device footprint and weight, and optimize data gathering in increasingly challenging environmental conditions (for example, underground, underwater and at high altitudes affixed to a drone, plane or space-based platforms).

claims.subject: Quantum Computing Inc.
claims.object_value: Quantum authentication / ZKP patent family (40+ countries, 2023)

claims.claim_text: QCi disclosed a going-concern doubt as of Dec 31, 2023: $2.06M cash, $19.94M annual operating cash burn, $1.44M working-capital deficit, $149.7M accumulated deficit; auditor (BF Borgers CPA PC) issued going-concern paragraph.
claims.subject: Quantum Computing Inc.
claims.object_value: $2.06M cash vs. $19.94M annual burn; going concern paragraph from BF Borgers
claims.source_quote: Our independent registered public accounting firm included an explanatory paragraph in its report on our financial statements as of and for the year ended December 31, 2023, noting the existence of substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.

claims.claim_text: Counterparty-disclosure control: do any major DoD prime contractors (Lockheed, Northrop, Raytheon, L3Harris, GD, Boeing, Honeywell) disclose Quantum Computing Inc. / QPhoton / QCi as a supplier, partner or named subcontractor in their own 10-Ks?
claims.subject: Major DoD primes
